--- PART 1/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "We have measurements from controlled probes starting with ten CC then 24 rounds. They test reactions to defection patterns. Parent has issues: four_D_TFT score 0.9458 (bad, mutual defection forever)."
STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional cooperator with streak-based retaliation and endgame exploitation; probes simulate one/four initial defections followed by TFT, four defections then ALLC, sustained defection, and periodic defection; the trace proposes adding forgiveness after long defection streaks and earlier exploitation of non-responsive opponents.

--- PART 2/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The measurements are only for the parent (slot 4). We don't have slot 11's probe scores. But we can infer from its code."
STRATEGY: The parent (slot 4) is a complex strategy that cooperates by default, retaliates against defections, and exploits near the end. The trace simulates the parent and slot 11 against probes like one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, and periodic_D. It proposes changing the parent by adding forgiveness after three consecutive opponent defections to fix the four_D_TFT probe score.

--- PART 3/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The probes measure scores over 34 rounds (10 CC + 24). They don't include the endgame (since only 34 rounds). The endgame behavior is not measured in these probes. The probes are specifically testing recovery and exploitation in the mid-game."
STRATEGY: The parent uses a heuristic that defects in the last 12 rounds if coop_rate > 0.6, and slot 11 uses a more conservative endgame rule. The trace simulates probe scores over 34 rounds (10 CC + 24) for one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. It changes the strategy by adding forgiveness after 3 or 4 consecutive opponent defections, periodic detection/exploitation, and a revised endgame.

--- PART 4/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: "This is terrible! We get stuck in an alternating exploitation cycle."; "This is a disaster."; "So we got into alternating exploitation."; "This is the same alternating cycle we saw earlier! Why?"; "So we get alternating 5,0,5,0."; "So we get stuck in DD. That's bad."
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's random 0.7 punishment gave 2.69 on one_D_TFT and 0.94 on four_D_TFT."; "Parent got 0.94 because it never forgave. So this is a huge improvement."; "Parent got 2.7083 (total ~92). So about same."
STRATEGY: The parent uses probabilistic punishment for single defections, deterministic punishment for longer streaks, and a conservative endgame. The trace simulates the parent and modified variants against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, and periodic_D. It changes the streak-defection rule to forgive at run_d==3 (and later considers always cooperating at run_d>=3) to fix four_D_TFT while preserving one_D_TFT performance.

--- PART 5/5 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's 0.7 punish was better than always punish, but always forgive is even better for these two probes." / "So we should definitely forgive single defection!"
STRATEGY: Parent is a conditional strategy that cooperates when opponent has no defections, defects when opponent has no cooperations, and otherwise reacts to opponent's last action and defection run-length. The trace simulates it against one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D, and grim trigger. It changes the last=='D' branch to forgive single defections unless overall defection rate is high, and to test at run==3 and continue cooperation at run==4 if its own last action was C.
